mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for three consecutive months signals labor market weakness and reduced consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% for 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not predict negative 60-day returns (e.g., Rank IC < 0.03) or negative returns occur in less than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing weakness and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, INDPRO declines below 95.0 do not lead to negative 5-day returns (e.g., Rank IC < 0.05) or returns are positive in more than 55% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth does not predict positive 20-day returns (e.g., Rank IC < 0.05) or returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with rising HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annualized CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL 12-month change exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate labor market deterioration, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement of UNRATE rising and PAYEMS falling does not predict negative 5-day returns (e.g., Rank IC < 0.03) or negative returns occur in less than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% signals aggressive policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS above 2.0% does not lead to negative 60-day returns (e.g., Rank IC < 0.05) or returns are positive in more than 55% of such cases.
